title: Fasting: deadly or what?
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss fasting: its etymology from the Old English "fastin," religious fasting across Buddhism, Catholicism, Eastern Orthodoxy, Judaism (Yom Kippur), Mormonism, and Islam (Ramadan), and the Australian Forty Hour Famine. They cover medical fasting before blood tests and surgery (including the rationale for pre-anesthesia fasting), the body's response to starvation (muscle and heart breakdown, starvation mode and metabolism), fasting for weight loss and its risks, detox cleanses and enemas, ketosis and halitosis, the eight-glasses-of-water myth, and political hunger strikes (Gandhi, Bobby Sands). The episode closes with a note on anorexia and unrealistic model images, then listener mail about a South by Southwest party and an Australian weight-loss challenge.

segments.title: Opening banter and fasting etymology
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about heartburn, diet, and pizza, then Josh introduces fasting and its Anglo-Saxon root word 'fastin'.

segments.title: Religious fasting: hallucinations and purpose
segments.summary: The hosts describe religious fasting as a way to get closer to God or atone for sins, and discuss claims that long fasts cause hallucinations, which may be interpreted as spiritual experience.

segments.title: Fasting in Buddhism, Catholicism, and Australia's Forty Hour Famine
segments.summary: Buddhist fasting on full moon days involves abstaining from solids but allowing broth. Catholic fasting on Ash Wednesday, Good Friday, and Lent is discussed, including school rice lunches, and the Australian Forty Hour Famine is introduced.

segments.title: Eastern Orthodox, Yom Kippur, and Mormon fasting
segments.summary: Eastern Orthodox fasts avoid meat, dairy, eggs, and fish. Jewish Yom Kippur fasting lasts about 25 hours with no food or drink. Mormons fast two meals on the first Sunday of each month and give the saved money to the needy.

segments.title: Ramadan
segments.summary: Muslims fast from sunrise to sunset for the month of Ramadan, commemorating the revelation of the Koran to Mohammed, abstaining from food, drink, smoking, cursing, and sex.

segments.title: Medical fasting before tests and surgery
segments.summary: Doctors ask patients to fast before blood tests so baseline cholesterol and blood sugar are accurate. Pre-surgery fasting is explained as a way to prevent vomiting and choking under anesthesia, a practice that may be phased out. The hosts also clarify nauseous versus nauseated.

segments.title: Starvation mode, muscle and heart damage, and fasting for weight loss
segments.summary: Without protein the body breaks down muscle, including the heart, and the liver and kidneys can shrink. Starvation mode lowers metabolism, making fasting for weight loss counterproductive and unhealthy. Beyonce's Master Cleanse is mentioned.

segments.title: Detox cleanses, ketosis, water myth, and hunger strikes
segments.summary: The hosts discuss detox cleanses and enemas as risky, ketosis and bad breath, debunk the eight-glasses-of-water rule, and cover political hunger strikes by Gandhi and Bobby Sands.

segments.title: Anorexia note, listener mail, and sign-off
segments.summary: Brief discussion of anorexia and unrealistic model images, then listener mail about a South by Southwest party in Austin and an Australian weight-loss challenge team, followed by the sign-off.
